group_assessment.weighting: Retrospective ancillary cohort of 77 children (mean age 8.5 years; 47 organic disease including 9 neurologic and one mitochondrial cytopathy, 30 anorexia nervosa) given a continuous exclusive enteral refeeding protocol, 3-week outcomes, no comparison arm. The reported fact is the incidence of laboratory and clinical complications under that protocol; effectiveness cannot be judged without a comparator, as the authors say. It is a class-level reference for refeeding risk with careful low-start enteral feeding, not a dextrose-solution or fluid-volume study and not WWOX.

entries.proposition: Ancillary retrospective analysis of 77 severely undernourished children (47 organic disease, 30 anorexia nervosa) given a standardised enteral refeeding protocol at one university hospital, with 3 weeks of follow-up.
entries.snippet: A total of 77 patients from the PREDIRE study were included (Figure 1); their mean ± SD age was 8.52 ± 6.3 years and 46 (59.7%) were girls (Table 1).

entries.proposition: The protocol started at a low intake relative to other pediatric protocols, about a third of the 30-40 kcal/kg/day used in comparison studies.
entries.snippet: the three times lower initial caloric intake of our protocol compared with the previous studies (10 vs. 30–40 kcal/kg/day, or 1860–1900 kcal/day)

entries.proposition: Supplement S1 gives the protocol: continuous exclusive enteral feeding over 24 h, 10 kcal/kg/d on day 1, oral phosphorus 1 mmol/kg/d for 10 days, oral thiamine 100 or 300 mg for 3 days, hydrolysed formula.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Supporting Information 1 (supplement docx): modality continuous exclusive EN over 24 hours; oral intake limited to 5 x 5 ml of milk; caloric intake D1 start with 10 kcal/kg/d; oral phosphorus 1 mmol/kg/d for 10 days; vitamin B1 3 days oral, 100 mg for younger children and 300 mg for older children.

experimental_context.system: pediatric enteral refeeding protocol, Lyon university hospital

entries.proposition: The enteral protocol was described as safe, with refeeding syndrome in 10.4% (8 of 77) by the ASPEN definition.
entries.snippet: According to the ASPEN definition, during the 3‐weeks refeeding period, the prevalence of RS in the total cohort was 10.4% (8/77 children).
entries.anchor: Results, RS: type, frequency, and delay

entries.proposition: Just before, the same paragraph says 19 children had one electrolyte abnormality, six had two and none three; eight with refeeding syndrome do not follow from six with two abnormalities, so the definition applied is not reproducible from the text.
entries.snippet: Overall, 19 (24.1%) children had only one abnormality, six (7.8%) had two, and none had three.
entries.anchor: Results, RS: type, frequency, and delay

entries.proposition: Hypophosphatemia (below 0.8 mmol/L) occurred in 13.7% during refeeding but symptomatic in 2.5%.
entries.snippet: but real hypophosphatemia (<0.8 mmol/L) in 13.7% of children, with only 2.5% of them presented with symptoms

entries.proposition: Peripheral edema during refeeding occurred in 6.7% (5/75), between days 2 and 21.
entries.snippet: Peripheral edema occurred in 6.7% of children, between Days 2 and 21.
entries.anchor: Results, RS: type, frequency, and delay

entries.proposition: Neurologic signs occurred in 4%, including hallucinations with severe hypophosphatemia (0.42 mmol/L) in one child with anorexia nervosa.
entries.snippet: 1 AN presented auditory and visual hallucination on Day 3 associated with a severe hypophosphatemia (0.42 mmol/L)
entries.anchor: Results, RS: type, frequency, and delay

entries.proposition: Hypoglycaemia (below 3.3 mmol/L) was present at inclusion in 22.2% overall and in 37.9% of the anorexia nervosa group, before refeeding.
Exclusion criteria listed premature stop of the protocol, yet 14 children (18.2%) interrupted early and are analysed.
entries.snippet: Exclusion criteria were missing medical record, parental refusal of inclusion, deviation from the enteral protocol (change in calories, premature stop).

entries.proposition: A premature interruption of the protocol occurred in 14 children, mostly for digestive intolerance.
entries.snippet: Over the 3‐week study period, a premature interruption or suspension of the protocol occurred in 14 (18.2%) children, between Days 1 and 16.
entries.anchor: Results, RS: type, frequency, and delay

entries.proposition: Weight-for-height rose from 72% to 82% in three weeks with half of the children still severely undernourished; the difference in weekly gain between anorexia nervosa and organic disease was 0.49% per week.
entries.snippet: During refeeding, WHR gain each week was significantly higher for AN with a difference of 0.49% of WHR gain higher each week for AN compared to OD (p = 0.033).

entries.proposition: The authors note that single-centre retrospective design, exclusion of intensive-care patients, and absence of follow-up after three weeks limit conclusions.
entries.snippet: First, its single‐center nature may limit the generalizability of the findings, we excluded patients from neonatal and pediatric intensive care which are at high RS risk.

entries.proposition: The authors say they cannot conclude on true effectiveness without more comparable studies and randomised comparisons.
entries.snippet: we need studies more comparable in terms of initial nutritional status and similar etiologies to conclude on the true effectiveness of renutrition.
